title: Moonlight Sentry — late shift follow-up log
content:
Shift window: 2026-06-11 22:00 UTC -> 2026-06-12 06:00 UTC
Owner (this doc): Priya Nair (priya@redwood.ai)
Relief oncall: Daniel Ortiz at 06:00 UTC
Slack channel: #sre-oncall, escalation @oncall-lead if pager after 2 pages

TL;DR
- Two customer-impacting incidents during the window; both mitigated to degraded service within 18 minutes.
- Main risk: prefix KV cache thrashing on specific long-history chat workloads -> elevated token latency and backend GPU cold-starts.
- Runbook gaps identified for KV cache size autosizing and for emergency routing to Dedicated fallback pool.
- Action items listed at the bottom with owners and short deadlines.

INCIDENTS
1) INC-2026-1789 — elevated token latency from 23:05 -> 23:23 UTC (mitigated)
   Symptoms: 95th/99th token latency spike for hosted-api model rwd-gpt-large in us-west-2. Observed >800ms per-token at 99th. Error rate for streaming connections increased from 0.1% -> 1.4%.
   Detection: alert from latency-slo-service (pager at 23:07).
   Immediate mitigation applied:
     - Disabled prefix prefetching for rwd-gpt-large traffic via runtime toggle (roll-back safe flag): Priya acted at 23:10.
     - Forced LRU eviction of KV cache shards with highest churn: Samir executed cache-evict script (ops/runbooks/kv-evict.sh) at 23:13.
     - Traffic temporarily routed to model variant rwd-gpt-large-compact for heavy sessions (automated fallback executed at 23:16).
   Outcome: token latency returned to baseline by 23:22. No customer data loss.
   Notes: Root cause likely long-context chat sessions (seq len > 16k) causing repeated KV cache thrashing and memory pressure that triggered slower kernel paths on certain GPU nodes.

2) Reduced batch throughput for embeddings bulk job — 02:40 -> 03:02 UTC (mitigated)
   Symptoms: Throughput drop on dedicated-pool-3 for embedding-ada-v2 where throughput fell by ~45%.
   Detection: alert from pool-health (>30% deviation) and one customer support ticket reporting slow ingest.
   Immediate mitigation applied:
     - Increased pool autoscale headroom (manual bump) and drained one unhealthy node: Lena performed node-drain + replace at 02:50.
     - Re-enabled optimistic batching heuristics after a temporary disable (toggle reverted at 02:55).
   Outcome: throughput back to expected by 03:00. Customer ticket updated; CS notified.

Auxiliary observations (non-impacting but worth noting)
- Several noisy alerts for ephemeral infra (spot eviction warnings) that contributed to alert fatigue. Consider lowering noise threshold or adding alert suppression for known maintenance windows.
- One non-user-facing microservice (metrics-relay) emitted repeated 5xx during the window; auto-restart handled by k8s, but runbook should include a quick verification step to confirm metrics continuity.

RUNBOOK GAPS & SUGGESTED CHANGES
- KV cache autosizing: current doc (confluence link in linked_artifacts) assumes static shard counts. Need a quick decision flow for when to (a) increase shard size, (b) evict aggressively, or (c) route to compact model variant.
  Suggested: add a sub-runbook with thresholds: if per-shard evictions/sec > 100 for 2m AND token-99-latency > 500ms then trigger compact-model-fallback and evict top-3 shards.
- Fallback routing: documented fallback bucket doesn't include dedicated-pool routing steps; add explicit sled to move traffic to Dedicated or to rwd-gpt-*compact variants with step-by-step commands and expected latency tradeoffs.
- Emergency contact matrix: make on-call escalation for Dedicated pool owners explicit (we hit hand-off ambiguity at 02:45).
- Add a short checklist for metrics-relay verification after auto-restart: run `curl` to metrics endpoint, confirm series continuity in grafana for last 10m.

KNOWN RISK ITEMS
- Memory growth patterns on some GPU node images (kernel path fallback under memory pressure). Ops imaging team owns a deeper follow-up to test workloads +/- quantization: ticket JIRA-SRE-4821 assigned to Samir.
- Backpressure: our optimistic batching heuristics can oversubscribe GPUs for embeddings bursts — risk when combined with spot termination windows. Consider conservative initial limits for bulk ingestion customers.

ACTION ITEMS (short list)
- SRE-4821: Deep investigation on KV cache thrash + repro harness. Owner: Samir Gupta. Target: 2026-06-18.
- Update runbook: add compact-model-fallback checklist + explicit routing to Dedicated. Owner: Daniel Ortiz. Target: 2026-06-14.
- Add metrics-relay sanity step to restart runbook and create a tiny verification script. Owner: Lena Brooks. Target: 2026-06-13.
- CS follow-up: confirm with affected customer(s) that performance returned to baseline and offer a brief post-incident note. Owner: Priya Nair (coord). Target: 2026-06-12 EOD.
- Alert tuning: suppress spot-eviction delta noise during maintenance windows; propose thresholds. Owner: eng-sre-alerting (proposal at next weekly sync). Target: 2026-06-17.

Handover checklist for incoming oncall (Daniel)
- Confirm INC-2026-1789 is assigned in PagerDuty with owner and that postmortem ticket exists.
- Verify SRE-4821 is visible and has initial repro notes in the ticket.
- Check Dedicated pool health dashboards (dedicated-pool-3) and confirm node replacement status.
- Head to #sre-oncall and update status with summary lines below.

Notes-to-self / informal bits
- If latency flares again, try the lighter-weight cache-evict first before disabling prefix prefetch; the latter causes transient quality deltas.
- Remember to attach heap profiles and GPU mem stats to SRE-4821. I collected the nvprof logs and put them in the incident artifacts folder (internal link in ticket).

References & helpful commands
- Cache eviction script: ops/runbooks/kv-evict.sh
- Fallback toggle command: runtime-toggle set model-prefetch=false --env hosted-prod --service inference
- Verify metrics continuity: curl -s "http://metrics-relay.internal/api/health" | jq .status

Final status at handover (06:00 UTC):
- All customer-facing services at baseline latency. No open pages.
- Action items created and owners assigned.

If anything flares immediately after handover: escalate to @oncall-lead, then to ENG-SRE pager chain.

End-of-doc.
